title: SparseInfer: Training-free Prediction of Activation Sparsity for Fast LLM Inference
problem: Modern LLMs using SiLU activation show minimal sparsity; ReLU replacement induces sparsity but prior methods required training a separate predictor to estimate it.
motivation: Activation sparsity is critical for LLM inference optimization; removing the training overhead of sparsity predictors enables immediate deployment.
method: SparseInfer predicts which computations in language models can be skipped when using ReLU activation (where negative outputs become zero) without any training. It checks only whether each input and weight value is positive or negative—not the actual numbers—to decide if an activation will be zero and safe to skip. You can tune the predictor to be more or less aggressive, trading off how many operations you actually skip against the risk of incorrectly identifying which ones can be skipped.
key_novelty: It predicts which computations can be skipped in ReLU language models using only sign comparison of inputs and weights, without training a separate predictor.
contributions: Negligible accuracy loss within 1 percentage point
Adaptive conservativeness tuning for inference optimization
primary_theme: Training-free activation sparsity prediction for LLM inference
